newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to publish energy hike details within days.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to publish energy hike details within days.

text.p: The owners of Hungary's energy companies, including several western investors, are likely to learn how much their investments could yield in 1997 within one or two days, the government said on Thursday.

Hungary's industry minister has decided on the rates at which energy companies are allowed to raise their prices from January 1, Elemer Kiss, Secretary of State of the Prime Minister's Office, told a news conference.
"According to my knowledge, the ministry has worked out (the details of the energy price rise) and must announce the decree within one or two days in (the legal gazette) Magyar Kozlony," he said.

The government announced in November retail hikes of 24.5 percent for electricity and 18.8 percent for gas but did not define the margins which would be granted to energy producers and distributors, in which Western utilities invested over $2 billion last year.
A number of western investors, including Germany's RWE and Electricite de France, bought substantial stakes in Hungarian energy companies one year ago.

Certain investors expressed dissatisfaction over the January 1 price rises, postponed from October, saying the hikes would not provide the eight percent profit margin the government had promised them before privatisation.
Belgian utility Tractebel said it might even pull out of its investment in the power station Dunamenti.
